subject: Urgent: Significant p95/p99 latency degradation after model swap - Luminary Health
messages:
From: Jane Mitchell <jane.mitchell@luminaryhealth.com>
To: support@redwood.ai, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@luminaryhealth.com
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden p99 spikes after model swap - urgent

Hi team,

We started seeing a sharp increase in p95/p99 latencies on the Hosted API around 08:30 PT following the model swap to model-v2.4. The checkout flow and parts of our recommendation pipeline are timing out (504) intermittently. Our monitoring shows p95 went from ~120ms to ~760ms and p99 to ~1.8s for the endpoint that uses the hosted text generation route. Error rate also increased from 0.2% to ~2.7%.

We are in the middle of a high-traffic promotion and this is impacting live transactions. Can you please triage this as escalated and advise immediate mitigation (rollback or traffic split)? We gathered a short snapshot (attached).

Attachments: luminary_latency_snapshot_0814.csv

Thanks,
Jane Mitchell
Head of Platform Engineering
Luminary Health
From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Mitchell <jane.mitchell@luminaryhealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:27:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes after model swap - urgent

Jane —

Thanks for the quick flag and the snapshot. We’re treating this as an urgent escalation. I’ve looped in Rishi and Connor to lead the technical investigation and Marissa on the CS/impact side.

Immediate actions we’ll take in parallel:
- We will initiate a traffic split to roll back 90% of traffic to model-v2.3 (the previous stable) within the hour unless you’d prefer a full rollback.
- Engineering will collect flamegraphs and end-to-end traces for requests hitting the new variant to identify contention points.
- We’ll open a high-priority support ticket and provide minute-by-minute updates on the support thread.

Connor/Rishi — can you confirm if the canary A/B telemetry shows any kernel/quantization path regressions and whether an emergency rollback is safe from a state/kv cache perspective?

Marissa — please coordinate the go/no-go with Luminary and prepare a brief mutual action plan.

PR
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
From: connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jane Mitchell <jane.mitchell@luminaryhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 10:05:44 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes after model swap - urgent

Quick update from the runtime diagnostics:
- Canary A/B runs show that model-v2.4 (int8-quantized) exhibits a sharp increase in kernel scheduling latency once sequence lengths exceed ~280 tokens; this matches the traffic profile Jane attached.
- We observed elevated lock contention on the KV cache eviction path for the new execution kernel; end-to-end traces show tail latency jumps correlating with cache flushes.
- Memory footprint for v2.4 is ~11% higher on the host which may amplify GC pauses in our runtime.

Given the customer impact and current traffic, my recommendation is to execute an emergency rollback to v2.3 for the affected route and then run a controlled canary re-introduction with tighter sequence-length gating and a reduced concurrency cap.

Planned mitigation steps (engineering):
1) Emergency rollback of route to model-v2.3 (90% rollback via traffic-split) — target start 10:00 PT.
2) Disable auto-batching for the route for 30 minutes while rollback completes to reduce concurrent KV pressure.
3) Post-rollback: run a 5% canary for v2.4 with sequence-length guard and collect extended traces.

Attachments: canary-flamegraph.svg

Connor O'Brien
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Mitchell <jane.mitchell@luminaryhealth.com>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 10:20:02 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes after model swap - urgent

Jane —

So sorry for the disruption, and thank you for the rapid signal. We propose the following mutual action plan:
- 10:00 PT: Redwood executes a 90% rollback to model-v2.3 on the affected endpoint; expected restoration within 5-8 minutes.
- 10:10 PT: Redwood confirms p95/p99 telemetry and keeps a 10% canary on v2.4 for monitoring.
- 10:30 PT: Post-rollback call to review traces and agree next steps for a safe re-rollout.

Would you like Redwood to proceed with the rollback at 10:00 PT? We can also do a full rollback if you prefer — we recommend the traffic-split first to minimize side effects.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Jane Mitchell <jane.mitchell@luminaryhealth.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 10:24:11 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes after model swap - urgent

Marissa / team —

Please proceed with the 90% traffic rollback at 10:00 PT. Business impact: our checkout conversion dropped ~12% in the last 30 minutes during the promotion — this needs to be fixed asap. We approve the rollback and the post-rollback diagnostics.

Thanks for the rapid coordination,
Jane
From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Jane Mitchell <jane.mitchell@luminaryhealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, connor_obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spikes after model swap - urgent

Jane —

Rollback completed at 10:06 PT. We confirmed p95/p99 returned to baseline within the expected window (p95 ~130ms, p99 ~210ms) for the affected route. We kept a 5% canary on v2.4 with sequence gating; no additional regressions seen after the gating change.

Immediate next steps:
- Engineering to produce a short postmortem with root cause, timeline, and rollout gating checklist (draft attached).
- Product to add sequence-length guard to rollout policy for quantized model variants.
- We will schedule a 30-minute review with Luminary next week to walk the postmortem and agree on a stable re-rollout plan.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-0814.md

We’ll keep this ticket open until Luminary gives final sign-off. Thank you for the quick approvals and patience.

PR
Priyom Das
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
